metadata.name: Tornado Risk Zones
metadata.description: Tornado Alley and Dixie Alley polygons approximating the commonly cited boundaries from meteorological literature. No official boundary exists for either concept.
sources: Gagan et al. (2010) 'A Historical and Statistical Comparison of Tornado Alley to Dixie Alley', NWA Digest Vol. 34 No. 2
Dixon et al. (2011) 'Tornado Risk Analysis: Is Dixie Alley an Extension of Tornado Alley?', Bull. Amer. Meteor. Soc. 92(4)
metadata.license: CC0 1.0 (coordinates derived from public domain scientific literature)
metadata.note: These are approximations. The scientific community agrees no universal definition exists.

properties.name: Tornado Alley
properties.description: Traditional Tornado Alley - central US corridor with highest tornado frequency. Based on NWS/SPC commonly cited boundaries: Rocky Mountain foothills to western Appalachians, from central Texas to the Dakotas.
properties.source: NWS Storm Prediction Center; Gagan et al. (2010) NWA Digest Vol. 34 No. 2
properties.definition_note: No official boundary exists. This polygon approximates the most commonly cited region.

properties.name: Dixie Alley
properties.description: Dixie Alley - southeastern US region with high tornado frequency and greater nighttime/off-season tornado risk. Coined by Dixon et al. (2001). Extends from eastern Texas through the Deep South.
properties.source: Dixon et al. (2001) 'Tornado Risk Analysis: Is Dixie Alley an Extension of Tornado Alley?', Bull. Amer. Meteor. Soc.; Purpura et al. NWS
properties.definition_note: No official boundary exists. This polygon approximates the most commonly cited region covering eastern TX, LA, AR, MS, AL, TN, KY, GA, northern FL.
